capabilities.description: Produce production module dependency facts for one completed, identified analysis while preserving canonical module ownership, behavioral classifications, counts, evidence, coverage and unavailable states.
uncertainties: The generated signature for analyzeDependencyDiagram has a cut documentation field, so the exact retained evidence shape and all existing result bounds need local engineering inspection.

capabilities.description: Answer a dependency request from one atomic published project revision and refuse or retry when the requested current input cannot be represented coherently.
uncertainties: The existing context history is explicitly bounded and process-local; it is evidence for coherent current-side selection, not durable baseline persistence.

capabilities.description: Persist, list, load and explicitly delete complete named dependency baselines for one canonical project, with atomic creation, duplicate-name refusal, compatibility metadata, corruption errors and configured storage limits.
uncertainties: The storage location, filename encoding, baseline-name rules, compatibility version and admission limits are not established by the request or generated evidence.

It is unresolved whether durable storage should remain directly in ramify/daemon or later warrant a child boundary; the map preserves the current tree because no concrete local-complexity evidence yet justifies one.

capabilities.description: Compare two identified dependency fact sets deterministically by canonical module and directed consumer/provider relationship, retaining before and after values, evidence and coverage while qualifying incomplete observations.
uncertainties: The exact comparison vocabulary for a relationship whose counts or classifications change is not yet defined.
The existing dependency fact evidence must be inspected to determine the smallest durable subset that preserves historical detail without retaining a full report or source tree.

capabilities.description: Expose one project-scoped save, list, delete and compare lifecycle to terminal and browser consumers while coordinating durable baselines with coherent current revisions.
uncertainties: The service vocabulary, cancellation behavior and boundary between daemon orchestration and contexts revision selection are not yet designed.

capabilities.description: Let a terminal user save, list, delete and compare named baselines, with readable output and deterministic JSON that identify both inputs, revisions, scope, coverage and qualified changes.
uncertainties: Command names, argument grammar and the stable JSON schema are not specified by the request.

capabilities.description: Project baseline lifecycle and comparison outcomes from the resident service into bounded browser data without scanning source or reconstructing dependency meaning.
uncertainties: The browser DTO size bound and whether historical detail is paged or separately requested are not established.

capabilities.description: Let a person select and manage a named baseline, request comparison against current analysis, refresh stale results and navigate to an individual dependency change.
uncertainties: The page state and interaction design for baseline selection, explicit deletion and stale refresh are not defined.

capabilities.description: Render added, removed and changed modules and directed relationships, including inspectable before and after evidence and clear historical, current, scope and incompleteness labels.
uncertainties: The request does not determine whether comparison is a mode of the existing dependency diagram or a distinct component within the project view.

relationships.reason: Both sides must use Ramify's existing production dependency meaning and fact classifications.
Both terminal and browser operations need the same durable project-scoped baseline collection.
Saving and comparing require one identified coherent current revision.
The shared service returns one comparison meaning to every surface.
Terminal lifecycle and comparison operations must use the same durable baselines as the browser.
The browser service projects shared operations and does not own persistence or analysis.
The explorer page needs bounded service state for lifecycle, comparison and staleness.
The explorer composes the pure comparison rendering and owns browser interaction state.

seams.agreementNeeded: Agree on the canonical, versioned, bounded dependency fact subset and identities that preserve module, relationship, classification, count, evidence and coverage meaning without retaining a whole analysis report.
Agree on how save and compare identify a single current revision, report supersession or retry, and expose staleness when a newer revision publishes.
Agree on project identity, name handling, duplicate, missing, corrupt, incompatible, interrupted and resource-limit outcomes shared by all clients.
Agree on deterministic module and relationship change records, before and after evidence, side-specific coverage and the distinction between definite and qualified observations.
Agree on lifecycle and comparison outcomes, identities and limits needed for human output and a deterministic JSON representation.
Agree on bounded browser operations and result states for baseline metadata, comparison detail, missing data, retry and staleness.
Agree on display-ready change identities, filters, totals, side labels, evidence provenance and detail retrieval without changing underlying comparison scope.

openQuestions: Does the existing dependency fact model retain enough bounded source evidence for both historical and current inspection, or must the baseline envelope add a stable evidence projection? This does not block identifying a bounded consumer goal; resolve it during local analysis engineering before fixing a storage schema.

What compatibility identities besides baseline format, project identity and dependency-analysis semantics must reject a comparison? This does not block identifying a bounded consumer goal; resolve it while defining the durable envelope.

What configured limits apply to baseline count, bytes per baseline, total storage and comparison result/detail size? This does not block identifying a bounded consumer goal, but every owning capability must preserve explicit refusal or incomplete outcomes.

Should durable baseline storage remain within ramify/daemon or become a child after its invariants and adapters are concrete? This does not block identifying a bounded consumer goal; preserving the current tree is the mapping recommendation.
Which surface is the initial bounded consumer is a stage-B decision and is intentionally unresolved by this capability map.
